requirement: Accept github:<owner>:<repo>:<path> and local:<alias>:<path>; require nonempty identity segments and valid GitHub owner/repository names. Paths use forward slashes; colon is reserved. Empty path is valid only for ls and means repository root.
Resolve github owner:repo through github.mappings first; otherwise use the GitHub API on github.com. Resolve local alias only through local.mappings. Do not infer identities from URLs.
Remote operations use the repository default branch unless --ref is supplied. Resolve the selected ref to one commit before reading paths; use that commit throughout the operation.

Reject absolute source paths and parent traversal. Local opens must enforce containment within the mapped root even if paths change concurrently. Reject symlink path components and nonregular file sources; skip symlinks and special files in listings. Remote reads and discovery must also exclude symlinks and submodules using Git tree entry types.

Read the single global CUE file ~/.gh-arrow unless --config overrides it. Never discover configuration in the working directory. Missing default config means no mappings; missing explicit config is an error. Empty config means no mappings.

Validate self-contained CUE against an embedded closed schema. Reject imports, malformed or incomplete values, unknown fields, duplicate repo mappings, empty identities and nonabsolute roots. Compare GitHub mapping identities case-insensitively. Limit configuration to 1 MiB and sanitize diagnostics. Never write configuration at runtime.

cp requires an existing destination parent; do not create directories. Reject directory or special-file destinations, destination symlinks and copying a file onto itself. Stage complete bytes in a private temporary file beside the destination; publish only after successful transfer. Refusal without --force must be race-safe. Failed copies preserve any existing destination and remove temporary files.
cat emits raw bytes only. cp emits no stdout on success. Send diagnostics to stderr.

ls outputs files only in lexicographic order with forward slashes and no headers or decoration. Paths are relative to the literal directory prefix before a glob; for a file operand return its basename.

Support * within a filename and ** as a complete recursive directory segment; ** includes zero directories. Reject ?, bracket patterns and embedded **. Directory-segment wildcards other than ** are unsupported.

A directory operand lists immediate files; a file operand lists that file. Empty directories and unmatched valid globs succeed with zero results; missing literal paths fail. Apply the same semantics locally and remotely.
Use API directory/tree enumeration rather than scraping GitHub pages. Detect truncated responses; complete enumeration or return an explicit incomplete-results error. Skip submodules and symlinks.
--org accepts an organization or user; enumerate all accessible repositories with pagination. Include archived repositories and forks; do not deduplicate forks.

Filter by exact topic when provided and check an exact nonempty file path relative to each repository root on its default branch. Reject globs. A directory at that path is a nonmatch for that repository. Do not fetch file contents.

Organization discovery always checks remote repositories and ignores local mappings. Include accessible private repositories through gh credentials. For user owners combine public owner enumeration with authenticated accessible repository enumeration filtered to that owner; the public user endpoint alone is insufficient. Visibility remains limited by the active credentials.
For discovery output owner/repo:path one per line sorted by owner/repo then path. No matches succeeds with empty output.
Never prompt or launch a browser during file operations. If authentication is needed, fail with guidance to run gh auth login separately. Do not expose credentials in diagnostics.
ls --json returns a JSON array of records as defined in listing.ts; empty result is []. Reject --json for cat and cp to protect byte-stream semantics.
Exit 0 for success including no matches; 1 for I/O, network, authentication, rate-limit or incomplete enumeration failures; 2 for invalid arguments, sources or configuration.
On enumeration failure return nonzero with no success listing on stdout; diagnostics identify the failing operation. Report rate limits without silently skipping repositories.

Use human-readable stderr messages prefixed by stable error codes: ARROW_USAGE, ARROW_CONFIG, ARROW_NOT_FOUND, ARROW_EXISTS, ARROW_PERMISSION, ARROW_AUTH, ARROW_NETWORK, ARROW_RATE_LIMIT, ARROW_INCOMPLETE, ARROW_IO.
Build a gh-arrow executable and publish precompiled release assets following GitHub CLI platform naming conventions. Document local build and gh extension install . once implementation exists.

Use GitHub.com explicitly for remote API access through gh credentials. Encode path and ref values as data; never interpolate them into shell commands. Never forward credentials to unrelated redirect hosts.

Escape control characters in text listings and diagnostics so each result occupies one line. JSON preserves path values using JSON escaping. cat remains an unmodified byte stream; a failed stream may contain partial bytes and must exit nonzero.

Use bounded request timeouts, retries and concurrency; support cancellation. API size or enumeration limits must produce a clear nonzero error unless a supported fallback completes the operation. Never silently truncate file bytes or listing results.
